summary: Cadenced Pulsar, powered by ASCIS (Autonomous Space Care Intelligence System), is an offline visual health companion that helps astronauts monitor their health by tracking vital signs, identifying unusual changes, and providing real-time visual feedback. By analyzing these health signals, it guide astronauts through the next steps when medical help from Earth is out of reach. This improves crew safety, autonomy, and mission resilience.
details: Our project combines space engineering, medical knowledge, and interactive technology to explore innovative solutions for challenges encountered during space missions. Through our original momentum-transfer tether concept, interactive 3D simulations, and accessible visual explanations, we aim to make complex scientific mechanisms easier to understand while exploring ways to improve the safety and efficiency of space exploration. We used Three.js (MIT License) to develop interactive 3D visualizations, Meshy to generate 3D models and visual assets, Canva to create storytelling videos, and the browser's built-in speech synthesis to provide voice output. Claude supported programming, text drafting, numerical recalculations, verification of calculations, and source summarization. Our project's creativity lies in connecting engineering, medicine, and digital storytelling to transform scientific ideas into engaging, interactive experiences. Throughout development, we considered scientific accuracy, medical reliability, accessibility, computational efficiency, cost, usability, and responsible AI integration. All original ideas, including the momentum-transfer tether, as well as the clinical content, medical decisions, scientific reasoning, and final review, were developed and carried out by our team. AI was used strictly as a supporting tool, with human judgment and oversight guiding every critical decision.
